transcript:
"This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour."
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
A senior White House official tells NPR that newly appointed press secretary Katie Zacharia
is out after less than five days on the job.
Earlier today, President Trump told reporters he had encouraged her to reconsider whether
she wanted the job.
"Katie's off to a start that the news has been so nasty to her.
I've never seen anything like it actually."
"Do you reconsider it?"
"And I said to her, 'Honestly, if I were you, I'd reconsider, you'd think about it,
but I wouldn't reconsider.'"
Zacharia faced scrutiny over how she has characterized her legal credentials.
During her first briefing on Tuesday, she took questions from only three reporters.
The FBI is assisting authorities in Oregon to determine a motive behind Thursday's mass
shooting at an elementary school.
Police say a 16-year-old shot through locked doors at Silver Rail Elementary, killing three
children and a teacher.
Sariah Sharp, whose 10-year-old attends the school, describes the confusion yesterday.
"It was just really confusing and hard to know what to believe.
I can only say it's not the worst day of my life because I got to see his face, but not
everybody got to see their loved ones."
The gunman was fatally shot by an armed bystander.
Despite powerful new ways to protect newborn babies against the respiratory virus, RSV,
many infants are still at risk, and PR's Rob Stein reports.
"RSV sends tens of thousands of babies to the hospital each year.
Many end up fighting for their lives in intensive care.
The best way to protect infants is to immunize newborns before they are discharged from hospitals.
But insurance companies typically won't pay for the shots in the hospital.
They're only required to pay for them in doctor's offices.
So about half of babies are being left unprotected against RSV, which is on the rise again right
now."
Rob Stein, NPR News.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is asking his European Union counterparts for
more support heading into winter.
Terry Schultz reports from Brussels.
Zelensky said he's counting on the EU for more assistance, as his relationship with
the Trump administration deteriorates, Russia continues to attack Ukraine's energy infrastructure,
and winter approaches.
"It's not only energy, it's also air defense and funding, and I'm thankful that EU stands
with us."
Some EU leaders are reportedly pressing Zelensky to rein in his criticism of Trump, but they're
also concerned the US ended its ban on Russian diesel imports, earning Moscow money.
EU leaders are again debating whether and how almost $250 billion worth of frozen Russian
assets can be used to fund Ukraine.
For NPR News, I'm Terry Schultz in Brussels.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Authorities in northwestern Pakistan have ordered inspections of all private schools
in the region.
The order is in response to a school roof collapse that killed 34 children and a teacher
this week.
Some victims' relatives say the building was already weak, and one says he had warned
the owner about leaks.
An order reviewed by the Associated Press says district inspection teams have three
days to submit their findings and recommendations.
President Trump is being cheered in Somaliland for praising the breakaway African state and
criticizing its parent nation, Somalia, and PR's Joel Bright reports.
Lots of people chanting "Victory to Somaliland" and "Long live America" gathered in Somaliland's
capital Hageza, waving American flags embezzled with images of President Trump.
This comes after Trump went on a tirade against Somalia during a campaign speech in Ohio
on Monday, saying Somalians did not have pants to wear, and that Somaliland, which broke
away from Somalia in 1999, was "a totally different country."
People at rallies say they hope Trump's comments could set the ball rolling for the U.S. to
recognize Somaliland as an independent nation, a move previous U.S. administrations have
rejected.
Joel Bright, NPR News, Lagos.
Stocks are trading sharply lower on Wall Street at this hour.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average is down 296 points, the Nasdaq down 657.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia out after less than five days on the job
FBI assisting Oregon authorities in determining motive for mass shooting at Silver Rail Elementary
Insurers typically won't cover RSV shots given in hospitals, leaving about half of babies unprotected
Zelensky asks EU for more energy, air defense, and funding support heading into winter
Authorities in northwestern Pakistan order inspections of private schools after roof collapse killed 34
Somaliland crowds cheer Trump's praise of breakaway state and criticism of Somalia
Wall Street stocks trading sharply lower, Dow down 296 points and Nasdaq down 657
